thread:
Mike: Heads up — did a quick spike on host-side tokenization + parsing overhead. baseline p95 decode went from 42ms -> 63ms after the kernel-selector change on canary. wondering if anyone else is seeing similar host CPU/serialize hit?
Irene: saw a tail bump in infra metrics around the same deploy window, might be related. what part of the pipeline is the hotspot? :thinking:
Mike: flamegraph points to two things: (1) tokenization + UTF8-normalize step (host CPU), (2) grpc write path where we do many small writes (lots of writev syscalls). kv cache lookups also show duplicate keys due to per-request parse rework.
Sasha: can you paste the pprof sample or the flame snippet?
Mike: pasted sample below (top stacks, aggregated):
- 24% host.tokenize.normalize_utf8
- 18% host.parse.http2_frame_assemble
- 12% host.stream.writev_many_small_writes
- 8% kvcache.lookup_duplicate_parses
- rest in model prep / scheduling
Irene: ugh writev thrash again. are we still doing single-chunk flush per token in stream mode?
Mike: currently we flush on each upstream chunk boundary, which for short tokens is tiny. suggestions: batch small writes for X ms or until size threshold.
Ben: we experimented with coalescing in April. setting COALESCE_WRITE_MS=5 and COALESCE_TARGET_BYTES=8192 cut syscall count ~3x in bench. but that added a ~2ms median for tiny responses. net p95 improved though.
Sasha: Tradeoff sounds fine if p95 improves. but the kernel-selector change earlier changed internal chunk size assumptions — we may be creating more fragments upstream, so coalescing becomes even more important.
PerfBot: perf-regression-alert: canary 2024-11-08 14:02 increased host cpu p95 by +50% for model-x-quant. Alert ID: pr-8421
Mike: confirm the canary above. I repro'd locally with sequence-length=8 workload where batching is low. attaching a short repro script:
```
# quick microbench
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  printf "\x00\x08msg-$i" | nc -q 0 localhost 7070
done
```
Sasha: try enabling ENABLE_STREAM_PREFETCH=yes and COALESCE_WRITE_MS=3 on the canary to see if it fixes writev noise. also set KVCACHE_PREFETCH=1 to dedupe lookups.
Mike: ran that — reduces writev syscalls ~2.5x and KV lookup rate down 18%. p95 dropped from 63ms -> 49ms, still above baseline.
Irene: remaining gap likely tokenization normalize. can we push a small change: move heavy unicode normalize step to sidecar / pre-tokenize stage? then host only receives already-normalized tokens.
Ben: sidecar will add a hop and network overhead. alternative: thin C-optimized normalize routine or use vectorized utf8 crate. bench numbers?
Mike: prototype C-impl (linked in my branch) cuts normalize time by ~60% on microbench (seq8). but integration risk is medium.
Sasha: another lever: batching heuristic — if seq_len <= 16 and model supports small-batch path, group incoming requests for up to 8ms to increase kernel utilization. that should amortize tokenize cost across requests.
Mike: agree. key is keeping latency SLO for single-shot callers. propose: canary config: BATCH_HOLD_MS=6, COALESCE_WRITE_MS=3, ENABLE_STREAM_PREFETCH=yes, KVCACHE_PREFETCH=1, USE_C_NORMALIZER=trial.
Irene: sounds good. add a fallback: if tail latency for single requests >12ms increase, rollback.
Ben: we'll need telemetry: per-request breakdown fields: tokenization_ms, parse_ms, writev_syscalls, kv_lookups. add those to console trace so we can split rollouts by route.
Mike: added a patch to add those traces to the /trace endpoint. example trace line: tokenization=5.2ms parse=1.1ms writev=14 kv_lookups=3
Sasha: one more note — grpc vs http2 framing differences. grpc path had extra header marshalling that doubled small-message overhead compared to plain http1 chunked. can we align codepaths more? maybe reuse the same framed buffer for both.
Mike: good catch. will unify framing buffer in host proxy. minimal change: share a single upstream buffer pool and only perform framing per batch instead of per-chunk.
PerfBot: benchmark-run queued: bench/model-x-seq8-coalesce-2024-11-09. results will post after run.
Irene: ok plan: (1) canary with coalesce + batching hold + kvprefetch + c-normalizer trial (2) add telemetry + tracing (3) run bench and post. if p95 back to baseline or better, promote.
Sasha: @Ben can you own the canary job and rollback rule?
Ben: on it. will create rollout with automatic rollback if single-request p95 increases >10% or error rate climbs.
Mike: thanks all. I'll open a very short runbook for oncall with the main knobs and quick rollback commands.
Irene: thx — also add instructions to toggle USE_C_NORMALIZER flag remotely in case we need to kill it fast.
Ben: rollout scheduled in 20m. PerfBot: ping when bench finishes. :rocket:
